passages.title: Asian chipmakers slide after Wall Street sell-off
passages.body: The sell-off in American AI stocks {{2026-11-23-ai-markets-spread}} to Asian markets as trading resumed on Monday. Shares in major South Korean chipmakers {{2026-11-23-ai-markets-declined}} by roughly three percent, weighing on the broader index. Chinese benchmarks also lost ground, although US stock futures later {{2026-11-23-ai-markets-rebounded}}. The mixed movements suggest investors were reassessing technology valuations rather than abandoning every AI-linked company.

passages.title: Climate summit ends without agreement in Turkey
passages.body: Climate negotiations in Turkey {{2026-11-23-climate-collapsed}} when the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed deal. The disagreement {{2026-11-23-climate-centred}} on whether governments should reaffirm an earlier pledge to move away from fossil fuels. European negotiators {{2026-11-23-climate-argued}} that weakening previous commitments would undermine the credibility of the talks. The failed summit exposed a persistent divide over how strongly countries should commit to reducing fossil-fuel dependence.

passages.title: British factories benefit from data-centre demand
passages.body: Demand for equipment used in data centres {{2026-11-23-britain-boosted}} British manufacturing activity to its strongest level in more than two years. The improvement partly {{2026-11-23-britain-offset}} slower expansion in the country's services sector. A preliminary business survey {{2026-11-23-britain-registered}} a November reading of 52.3, below October's 52.9. Because the index remained above 50, the figures still indicated overall private-sector growth.

passages.title: Naval-drone attack reaches a Libyan port
passages.body: A Russian warship was reportedly {{2026-11-23-libya-sunk}} in the Libyan port of Benghazi during a naval-drone attack. Ukraine's president {{2026-11-23-libya-claimed}} responsibility and praised the operation. The strike {{2026-11-23-libya-occurred}} in territory controlled by a Libyan force aligned with Russia. Kyiv had earlier reported targeting a Russian cargo vessel in the Baltic Sea, illustrating the widening geographic reach of its maritime operations.

passages.title: West Bank villages face renewed settler attacks
passages.body: Israeli settlers {{2026-11-23-westbank-attacked}} several Palestinian villages near Ramallah, setting vehicles alight and marking buildings with graffiti. An Israeli opposition leader {{2026-11-23-westbank-condemned}} the violence and accused nationalist ministers of encouraging it. The latest incidents {{2026-11-23-westbank-intensified}} concerns about the safety of Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank. Reports of settler violence have grown increasingly severe since the October 2023 attacks and subsequent war.

passages.title: A commanding Democratic majority in Congress
passages.body: Democrats {{2026-11-23-house-secured}} their 258th seat in the US House after a North Carolina contest was decided in their favour. The result {{2026-11-23-house-gave}} the party a majority of at least 85 seats, an unusually wide margin by recent historical standards. Four congressional races {{2026-11-23-house-remained}} unresolved nearly three weeks after the midterm elections. The outstanding contests could alter the final tally without changing which party controls the chamber.

passages.title: Jewellery house remembers a family pioneer
passages.body: Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari {{2026-11-23-bulgari-died}} at the age of 89 after decades in the family luxury business. He {{2026-11-23-bulgari-joined}} the company in 1960 and developed a reputation for expertise in precious stones. His family later {{2026-11-23-bulgari-sold}} its stake to French luxury group LVMH in 2011. His career helped transform a business founded by his grandfather into an internationally recognised jewellery brand.
